name: Number of distinct exponents in the prime factorization of n!.
comment: Erdős proved that there exist two constants c1, c2 > 0 such that c1 (n / log(n))^(1/2) < a(n) < c2 (n / log(n))^(1/2). - _Carlo Sanna_, May 28 2019

R. Heyman and R. Miraj proved that the cardinality of the set { floor(n/p) : p <= n, p prime } is same as the number of distinct exponents in the prime factorization of n!. - _Md Rahil Miraj_, Apr 05 2024

example: n=7: 7! = 5040 = 2*2*2*2*3*3*5*7; three different exponents arise: 4, 2 and 1; a(7)=3.
n=7: { floor(7/p) : p <= 7, p prime } = {3,2,1}. So, its cardinality is 3. - _Md Rahil Miraj_, Apr 05 2024
